title: Which digits solve EF times E and WOW times five?
description: Two letter puzzles from the book are solved. The first uses the fact that a repeated digit number like GGG is one hundred and eleven times G, and one hundred and eleven is three times thirty seven. The second uses the last digits of multiples of five.
teaching_notes: One idea: a repeated digit number like GGG is one hundred and eleven times G, and one hundred and eleven is three times thirty seven. Watch for children who accept a solution where two letters share a digit.

video_script.why: The child has solved small letter puzzles with size and last digits, and now uses a factor of GGG and the last digits of multiples of five.
video_script.substitution: Rewrite GGG as one hundred and eleven times G and look for the factor thirty seven; for the second, use what five times a digit can end in.
video_script.anchor: the two letter puzzles of the book: EF × E = GGG and WOW × 5 = MEOW
video_script.payoff_line: Five hundred and seventy five times five is two thousand eight hundred and seventy five.

final_answer.spoken: thirty seven times three is one hundred and eleven, and five hundred and seventy five times five is two thousand eight hundred and seventy five

never_show: 525 × 5 = 2625 as a solution, marked as right
maths_rules: (i) GGG = 111 × G = 3 × 37 × G; E is one digit, so 37 must divide EF
two digit multiples of 37: 37 and 74; E is the tens digit, so E = 3 or E = 7
37 × 3 = 111: G = 1, E = 3, F = 7, all different; 74 × 7 = 518, not a repeated digit
(ii) 5 × W ends in W: 5 × 5 = 25 ends in 5, 5 × 0 = 0 ends in 0; W is a first digit, so W = 5
5O5 × 5 = 2525 + 50 × O; tens digit of the answer is 2 when O is even and 7 when O is odd; it must equal O, so O = 2 or O = 7
525 × 5 = 2625: M = 2 and O = 2, a repeat, ruled out
575 × 5 = 2875: M = 2, E = 8, O = 7, W = 5, all different
video_script.design: One idea: rewrite repeated digits as one hundred and eleven times a digit, and use the last digits of multiples of five. The two puzzles stay on the board as the anchor. The check puts the digits back.

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, take E F times E equals G G G. G G G is one hundred and eleven times G.
<bookmark mark='fac'/>One hundred and eleven is three times thirty seven, so thirty seven is a factor.
<bookmark mark='single'/>E is a single digit, so thirty seven must divide E F.
<bookmark mark='two'/>E F has two digits, so it is thirty seven or seventy four.

marks.res: E = 3, F = 7 and G = 1 are written

beats.colours: the crossed choice in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='t37'/>Step two, test thirty seven. Its tens digit is three, so E is three.
<bookmark mark='p1'/>Thirty seven times three is one hundred and eleven, and then G is one.
<bookmark mark='t74'/>Next test seventy four. Its tens digit is seven, so E is seven.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>Seventy four times seven is five hundred and eighteen, which is not a repeated digit.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Then E is three, F is seven and G is one.

narration: <bookmark mark='w'/>Step three, take W O W times five equals M E O W. Five times W ends in W.
<bookmark mark='w5'/>That happens for W as zero or five, and W cannot be zero, so W is five.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Five O five times five is two thousand five hundred twenty five plus fifty times O.
<bookmark mark='oe'/>For even O the last two digits are twenty five. For odd O they are seventy five.
<bookmark mark='oo'/>The tens digit of the answer is O, so O is two or seven.
